astreon.description: Workout sheet manager built as a real product — multi-tenant, with evolution history and a structure that grows with the user.
astreon.previewDesc: Some screens of Astreon in action.
astreon.problemDesc: Astreon was born from a real daily pain — workout sheets noted on WhatsApp that got lost in the history, with no record of weights, reps or week-to-week progress. No rest timer between sets, no training time history, no way to know what worked.
problemItems: No record of weights or week-to-week progress
Old sheets inaccessible — no way to know what worked
Hard to adapt workouts as you progress
astreon.whatDesc: Astreon is a simple and complete workout sheet manager. Organizes workouts, tracks progress and keeps history — without relying on WhatsApp, notes or memory. Planned from the start as a multi-tenant product, aiming to serve both beginners and personal trainers.

howFlows.title: Creating a workout sheet
steps: User creates a new sheet with a name and lifetime period
Splits into days/groups (Workout A, B, C / Upper, Lower, etc.)
For each day, adds exercises with weight, reps and rest time
Can add specific notes per exercise

howFlows.title: Workout Mode (at the gym)
steps: Opens the active sheet and selects the day
General timer starts counting gym time
For each completed set, rest timer starts automatically
Notes during the workout (e.g. 'increased weight today')
When done: total time recorded, notes saved to history

howFlows.title: Reviewing history
steps: Access previous sheets filtered by month or period
View each training day with its notes
Track progress in weights, time and volume over time

howFlows.title: Sheet lifecycle
steps: App tracks the period defined at creation
Alert when sheet is close to expiring
When expired, suggests creating a new sheet and archives the old one automatically

nebula.description: CLI for project scaffolding with opinionated templates — skip the boilerplate, start with what matters.
nebula.problemDesc: Every new project starts the same way: configure TypeScript, add auth, connect ORM, create a global error handler, organize the folder structure. Hours of setup before writing a single line of code that actually matters — and always the same way.
nebula.whatDesc: Nebula was born as a personal tool: an interactive CLI that generates complete projects with a single command, done right from the start. Opinionated by design — because the best tools have a point of view.

ecommerce.description: E-commerce REST API built as a learning and portfolio project, focused on backend organization, data validation, and relational persistence.
ecommerce.problemDesc: An e-commerce workflow needs to keep users, catalog, orders, and stock consistent. This API brings these operations together through organized endpoints and applies core rules on the server instead of trusting values sent by the client.
ecommerce.whatDesc: A REST API built with NestJS and Fastify, using PostgreSQL for persistence and Prisma for data access. Modules are separated by domain, and services depend on repository contracts to keep business logic separate from persistence implementation.
featureItems: CRUD for users, categories, and products
Filter products by category and partial name
Create and retrieve orders, with optional user filtering
Server-side total calculation and unit-price snapshot at purchase time
Stock deduction when creating an order and restoration on cancellation
Data and environment validation with Zod
Password hashing with Argon2 and global exception handling
ecommerce.architectureDesc: The application is organized into domain modules and uses the Repository pattern to separate services from persistence. Order operations use transactions to keep order and stock data consistent.
ecommerce.flow: Controller → Service → Abstract Repository → Prisma Repository → PostgreSQL
ecommerce.limitationsDesc: The project does not implement authentication or authorization. It was built to demonstrate backend concepts and should not be used in production with real data without the necessary protections.
ecommerce.endpointsDesc: Main operations available in the API, grouped by resource. Check the interactive documentation for parameters and response formats.
ecommerce.rulesDesc: Order totals are calculated on the server, unit prices are preserved at purchase time, and stock changes are handled within transactions. Stock is restored only when an order is successfully cancelled, preventing duplicate restocking.
